mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the predicted negative returns are not statistically distinguishable from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a rise in unemployment (UNRATE) above 5% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 70% of triggered episodes, or the correlation between the trigger and subsequent returns is not statistically significant at the 95% level.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered periods (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months signals a contraction in economic output, which reduces corporate earnings and capital expenditure, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the predicted negative effect is not robust to a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in the housing starts index (HOUST) and personal savings rate (RSAFS) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a shift from savings to investment in housing, which boosts construction sector earnings and related equities, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during triggered periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate held below 2% for more than six consecutive months during a period of positive GDP growth (GDPC1) signals accommodative monetary policy that supports credit expansion and equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 2% AND GDPC1 growth > 0% for 6 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly payroll employment increase (PAYEMS) below the prior month for three consecutive months signals a deceleration in labor market momentum, which presages weaker consumer demand and lower corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered periods (t-test p > 0.20).

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) of less than 0.5% coupled with a stable unemployment rate (UNRATE) near historical lows signals resilient consumer demand despite mild economic headwinds, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.05).
